title: Peter and John before the Sanhedrin + the believers hold all things in common

paragraphs.text: And as they spake unto the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
paragraphs.original: Λαλούντων δὲ αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι,
paragraphs.translit: Lalountōn de autōn pros ton laon epestēsan autois hoi hiereis kai ho stratēgos tou hierou kai hoi Saddoukaioi,

paragraphs.text: being sore troubled because they taught the people, and proclaimed in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
paragraphs.original: διαπονούμενοι διὰ τὸ διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸν λαὸν καὶ καταγγέλλειν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
paragraphs.translit: diaponoumenoi dia to didaskein autous ton laon kai katangellein en tō Iēsou tēn anastasin tēn ek nekrōn,

paragraphs.text: And they laid hands on them, and put them in ward unto the morrow: for it was now eventide.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπέβαλον αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἔθεντο εἰς τήρησιν εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἦν γὰρ ἑσπέρα ἤδη.
paragraphs.translit: kai epebalon autois tas cheiras kai ethento eis tērēsin eis tēn aurion, ēn gar hespera ēdē.

paragraphs.text: But many of them that heard the word believed; and the number of the men came to be about five thousand.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ δὲ τῶν ἀκουσάντων τὸν λόγον ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ ἐγενήθη ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ὡς χιλιάδες πέντε.
paragraphs.translit: polloi de tōn akousantōn ton logon episteusan, kai egenēthē ho arithmos tōn andrōn hōs chiliades pente.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem;
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον συναχθῆναι αὐτῶν τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de epi tēn aurion synachthēnai autōn tous archontas kai tous presbyterous kai tous grammateis en Ierousalēm

paragraphs.text: and Annas the high priest [was there], and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest.
paragraphs.original: (καὶ Ἅννας ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ Καϊάφας καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος καὶ ὅσοι ἦσαν ἐκ γένους ἀρχιερατικοῦ),
paragraphs.translit: (kai Hannas ho archiereus kai Kaiaphas kai Iōannēs kai Alexandros kai hosoi ēsan ek genous archieratikou),

paragraphs.text: And when they had set them in the midst, they inquired, By what power, or in what name, have ye done this?
paragraphs.original: καὶ στήσαντες αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ μέσῳ ἐπυνθάνοντο· Ἐν ποίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ ἐν ποίῳ ὀνόματι ἐποιήσατε τοῦτο ὑμεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: kai stēsantes autous en tō mesō epynthanonto· En poia dynamei ē en poiō onomati epoiēsate touto hymeis;

paragraphs.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders,
paragraphs.original: τότε Πέτρος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ πρεσβύτεροι,
paragraphs.translit: tote Petros plēstheis pneumatos hagiou eipen pros autous· Archontes tou laou kai presbyteroi,

paragraphs.text: if we this day are examined concerning a good deed done to an impotent man, by what means this man is made whole;
paragraphs.original: εἰ ἡμεῖς σήμερον ἀνακρινόμεθα ἐπὶ εὐεργεσίᾳ ἀνθρώπου ἀσθενοῦς, ἐν τίνι οὗτος σέσωσται,
paragraphs.translit: ei hēmeis sēmeron anakrinometha epi euergesia anthrōpou asthenous, en tini houtos sesōstai,

paragraphs.text: be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, [even] in him doth this man stand here before you whole.
paragraphs.original: γνωστὸν ἔστω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν καὶ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου, ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε, ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐν τούτῳ οὗτος παρέστηκεν ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ὑγιής.
paragraphs.translit: gnōston estō pasin hymin kai panti tō laō Israēl hoti en tō onomati Iēsou Christou tou Nazōraiou, hon hymeis estaurōsate, hon ho theos ēgeiren ek nekrōn, en toutō houtos parestēken enōpion hymōn hygiēs.

paragraphs.text: He is the stone which was set at nought of you the builders, which was made the head of the corner.
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ λίθος ὁ ἐξουθενηθεὶς ὑφʼ ὑμῶν τῶν οἰκοδόμων, ὁ γενόμενος εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας.
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin ho lithos ho exouthenētheis hyphʼ hymōn tōn oikodomōn, ho genomenos eis kephalēn gōnias.

paragraphs.text: And in none other is there salvation: for neither is there any other name under heaven, that is given among men, wherein we must be saved.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία, οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομά ἐστιν ἕτερον ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸ δεδομένον ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἐν ᾧ δεῖ σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk estin en allō oudeni hē sōtēria, oude gar onoma estin heteron hypo ton ouranon to dedomenon en anthrōpois en hō dei sōthēnai hēmas.

paragraphs.text: Now when they beheld the boldness of Peter and John, and had perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Θεωροῦντες δὲ τὴν τοῦ Πέτρου παρρησίαν καὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ καταλαβόμενοι ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ἀγράμματοί εἰσιν καὶ ἰδιῶται, ἐθαύμαζον, ἐπεγίνωσκόν τε αὐτοὺς ὅτι σὺν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἦσαν,
paragraphs.translit: Theōrountes de tēn tou Petrou parrēsian kai Iōannou kai katalabomenoi hoti anthrōpoi agrammatoi eisin kai idiōtai, ethaumazon, epeginōskon te autous hoti syn tō Iēsou ēsan,

paragraphs.text: And seeing the man that was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
paragraphs.original: τόν τε ἄνθρωπον βλέποντες σὺν αὐτοῖς ἑστῶτα τὸν τεθεραπευμένον οὐδὲν εἶχον ἀντειπεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ton te anthrōpon blepontes syn autois hestōta ton tetherapeumenon ouden eichon anteipein.

paragraphs.text: But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves,
paragraphs.original: κελεύσαντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔξω τοῦ συνεδρίου ἀπελθεῖν συνέβαλλον πρὸς ἀλλήλους
paragraphs.translit: keleusantes de autous exō tou synedriou apelthein syneballon pros allēlous

paragraphs.text: saying, What shall we do to these men? for that indeed a notable miracle hath been wrought through them, is manifest to all that dwell in Jerusalem; and we cannot deny it.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες· Τί ποιήσωμεν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις; ὅτι μὲν γὰρ γνωστὸν σημεῖον γέγονεν διʼ αὐτῶν πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλὴμ φανερόν, καὶ οὐ δυνάμεθα ἀρνεῖσθαι·
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Ti poiēsōmen tois anthrōpois toutois; hoti men gar gnōston sēmeion gegonen diʼ autōn pasin tois katoikousin Ierousalēm phaneron, kai ou dynametha arneisthai·

paragraphs.text: But that it spread no further among the people, let us threaten them, that they speak henceforth to no man in this name.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ἵνα μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖον διανεμηθῇ εἰς τὸν λαόν, ἀπειλησώμεθα αὐτοῖς μηκέτι λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ hina mē epi pleion dianemēthē eis ton laon, apeilēsōmetha autois mēketi lalein epi tō onomati toutō mēdeni anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: And they called them, and charged them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καλέσαντες αὐτοὺς παρήγγειλαν τὸ καθόλου μὴ φθέγγεσθαι μηδὲ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai kalesantes autous parēngeilan to katholou mē phthengesthai mēde didaskein epi tō onomati tou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it is right in the sight of God to hearken unto you rather than unto God, judge ye:
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀποκριθέντες εἶπον πρὸς αὐτούς· Εἰ δίκαιόν ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν ἀκούειν μᾶλλον ἢ τοῦ θεοῦ, κρίνατε,
paragraphs.translit: ho de Petros kai Iōannēs apokrithentes eipon pros autous· Ei dikaion estin enōpion tou theou hymōn akouein mallon ē tou theou, krinate,

paragraphs.text: for we cannot but speak the things which we saw and heard.
paragraphs.original: οὐ δυνάμεθα γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἃ εἴδαμεν καὶ ἠκούσαμεν μὴ λαλεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ou dynametha gar hēmeis ha eidamen kai ēkousamen mē lalein.

paragraphs.text: And they, when they had further threatened them, let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them, because of the people; for all men glorified God for that which was done.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ προσαπειλησάμενοι ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς, μηδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τὸ πῶς κολάσωνται αὐτούς, διὰ τὸν λαόν, ὅτι πάντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ τῷ γεγονότι·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de prosapeilēsamenoi apelysan autous, mēden heuriskontes to pōs kolasōntai autous, dia ton laon, hoti pantes edoxazon ton theon epi tō gegonoti·

paragraphs.text: For the man was more than forty years old, on whom this miracle of healing was wrought.
paragraphs.original: ἐτῶν γὰρ ἦν πλειόνων τεσσεράκοντα ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐφʼ ὃν γεγόνει τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο τῆς ἰάσεως.
paragraphs.translit: etōn gar ēn pleionōn tesserakonta ho anthrōpos ephʼ hon gegonei to sēmeion touto tēs iaseōs.

paragraphs.text: And being let go, they came to their own company, and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said unto them.
paragraphs.original: Ἀπολυθέντες δὲ ἦλθον πρὸς τοὺς ἰδίους καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ὅσα πρὸς αὐτοὺς οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι εἶπαν.
paragraphs.translit: Apolythentes de ēlthon pros tous idious kai apēngeilan hosa pros autous hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi eipan.

paragraphs.text: And they, when they heard it, lifted up their voice to God with one accord, and said, O Lord, thou that didst make the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all that in them is:
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἦραν φωνὴν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπαν· Δέσποτα, σὺ ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς,
paragraphs.translit: hoi de akousantes homothymadon ēran phōnēn pros ton theon kai eipan· Despota, sy ho poiēsas ton ouranon kai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan kai panta ta en autois,

paragraphs.text: who by the Holy Spirit, [by] the mouth of our father David thy servant, didst say, Why did the Gentiles rage, And the peoples imagine vain things?
paragraphs.original: ὁ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου στόματος Δαυὶδ παιδός σου εἰπών· Ἱνατί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά;
paragraphs.translit: ho tou patros hēmōn dia pneumatos hagiou stomatos Dauid paidos sou eipōn· Hinati ephryaxan ethnē kai laoi emeletēsan kena;

paragraphs.text: The kings of the earth set themselves in array, And the rulers were gathered together, Against the Lord, and against his Anointed:
paragraphs.original: παρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: parestēsan hoi basileis tēs gēs kai hoi archontes synēchthēsan epi to auto kata tou kyriou kai kata tou christou autou.

paragraphs.text: for of a truth in this city against thy holy Servant Jesus, whom thou didst anoint, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, were gathered together,
paragraphs.original: συνήχθησαν γὰρ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον παῖδά σου Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ἔχρισας, Ἡρῴδης τε καὶ Πόντιος Πιλᾶτος σὺν ἔθνεσιν καὶ λαοῖς Ἰσραήλ,
paragraphs.translit: synēchthēsan gar epʼ alētheias en tē polei tautē epi ton hagion paida sou Iēsoun, hon echrisas, Hērōdēs te kai Pontios Pilatos syn ethnesin kai laois Israēl,

paragraphs.text: to do whatsoever thy hand and thy council foreordained to come to pass.
paragraphs.original: ποιῆσαι ὅσα ἡ χείρ σου καὶ ἡ βουλὴ προώρισεν γενέσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: poiēsai hosa hē cheir sou kai hē boulē proōrisen genesthai.

paragraphs.text: And now, Lord, look upon their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants to speak thy word with all boldness,
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν, κύριε, ἔπιδε ἐπὶ τὰς ἀπειλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ δὸς τοῖς δούλοις σου μετὰ παρρησίας πάσης λαλεῖν τὸν λόγον σου,
paragraphs.translit: kai ta nyn, kyrie, epide epi tas apeilas autōn kai dos tois doulois sou meta parrēsias pasēs lalein ton logon sou,

paragraphs.text: while thy stretchest forth thy hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done through the name of thy holy Servant Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τῷ τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐκτείνειν σε εἰς ἴασιν καὶ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ ἁγίου παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: en tō tēn cheira sou ekteinein se eis iasin kai sēmeia kai terata ginesthai dia tou onomatos tou hagiou paidos sou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And when they had prayed, the place was shaken wherein they were gathered together; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spake the word of God with boldness.
paragraphs.original: καὶ δεηθέντων αὐτῶν ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν συνηγμένοι, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἅπαντες τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, καὶ ἐλάλουν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρρησίας.
paragraphs.translit: kai deēthentōn autōn esaleuthē ho topos en hō ēsan synēgmenoi, kai eplēsthēsan hapantes tou hagiou pneumatos, kai elaloun ton logon tou theou meta parrēsias.

paragraphs.text: And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and soul: and not one [of them] said that aught of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common.
paragraphs.original: Τοῦ δὲ πλήθους τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν καρδία καὶ ψυχὴ μία, καὶ οὐδὲ εἷς τι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ ἔλεγεν ἴδιον εἶναι, ἀλλʼ ἦν αὐτοῖς πάντα κοινά.
paragraphs.translit: Tou de plēthous tōn pisteusantōn ēn kardia kai psychē mia, kai oude heis ti tōn hyparchontōn autō elegen idion einai, allʼ ēn autois panta koina.

paragraphs.text: And with great power gave the apostles their witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus: and great grace was upon them all.
paragraphs.original: καὶ δυνάμει μεγάλῃ ἀπεδίδουν τὸ μαρτύριον οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, χάρις τε μεγάλη ἦν ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai dynamei megalē apedidoun to martyrion hoi apostoloi tēs anastaseōs tou kyriou Iēsou, charis te megalē ēn epi pantas autous.

paragraphs.text: For neither was there among them any that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐνδεής τις ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς· ὅσοι γὰρ κτήτορες χωρίων ἢ οἰκιῶν ὑπῆρχον, πωλοῦντες ἔφερον τὰς τιμὰς τῶν πιπρασκομένων
paragraphs.translit: oude gar endeēs tis ēn en autois· hosoi gar ktētores chōriōn ē oikiōn hypērchon, pōlountes epheron tas timas tōn pipraskomenōn

paragraphs.text: and laid them at the apostles` feet: and distribution was made unto each, according as any one had need.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐτίθουν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων· διεδίδετο δὲ ἑκάστῳ καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai etithoun para tous podas tōn apostolōn· diedideto de hekastō kathoti an tis chreian eichen.

paragraphs.text: And Joseph, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, Son of exhortation), a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race,
paragraphs.original: Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἐπικληθεὶς Βαρναβᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον υἱὸς παρακλήσεως, Λευίτης, Κύπριος τῷ γένει,
paragraphs.translit: Iōsēph de ho epiklētheis Barnabas apo tōn apostolōn, ho estin methermēneuomenon hyios paraklēseōs, Leuitēs, Kyprios tō genei,

paragraphs.text: having a field, sold it, and brought the money and laid it at the apostles` feet.
paragraphs.original: ὑπάρχοντος αὐτῷ ἀγροῦ πωλήσας ἤνεγκεν τὸ χρῆμα καὶ ἔθηκεν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων.
paragraphs.translit: hyparchontos autō agrou pōlēsas ēnenken to chrēma kai ethēken para tous podas tōn apostolōn.
